title: Ask Before You Answer: A Question-Driven Evidence Reasoning Architecture (QERA) for In-Context Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.35083v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI assistants are increasingly asked to reason over a user's own web traces: group chats, community threads, activity logs and revision histories. On CL-bench Life, a benchmark of such real-life context learning, frontier LLMs solve fewer than one task in five. We find that the request is not the specification: over 80% of the benchmark's rubrics share less than 60% of their content words with the final request, as for a rule set two turns earlier or every record that meets the user's criterion, and LLMs answering directly pass only 67% of these implicit rubrics against 81% of the others. We propose QERA, a Question-driven Evidence Reasoning Architecture that asks before it answers. QERA first turns the request into a requirement checklist and typed information needs, filtered by code for faithfulness to the user's words; it then answers from the whole conversation, asks the same questions again with quotes verified by code, and applies

translated_title: 先问再答：面向上下文学习的问题驱动证据推理架构（QERA）
translated_abstract: AI助手越来越多地被要求基于用户自己的网络痕迹进行推理，包括群聊、社区帖子、活动日志和修订历史。在CL-bench Life这一真实生活上下文学习基准上，前沿大语言模型解决的任务不足五分之一。我们发现请求本身并非任务规范：该基准中超过80%的评分标准与最终请求的内容词重合度低于60%，例如两条对话之前的规则集，或所有满足用户某项标准的记录，而直接作答的大语言模型在这些隐含标准上仅通过67%，相比之下在其他标准上通过率为81%。我们提出QERA，一种先问再答的问题驱动证据推理架构。QERA首先将请求转化为需求清单和类型化的信息需求，并通过代码进行过滤以确保忠实于用户的原话；然后基于整个对话进行回答，使用经代码验证的引文再次提出相同的问题，并应用……（摘要内容在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出QERA架构，通过先将用户请求转化为需求清单并筛选出隐含信息需求，再从完整对话中作答并用代码验证引文，从而解决大语言模型在真实生活上下文学习任务中因请求隐含大量未明说标准而表现不佳的问题。
